answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity expensive and reputation slow to earn. Each agent posts a bond before trading, like an ember that only burns while staked: the bond sits in escrow and is slashed if peers prove duplicate identities or fabricated work. A new agent starts with a yarrow badge worth nothing, and only verified trades raise its standing, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand bonds and earn no trust. Accounts flagged violet by peer review lose their bond and start over, so attackers pay linearly for every identity while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
